title: Tristan Peters’ 18-pitch walk helps White Sox stay ahead of Guardians in AL Central
content:
CLEVELAND — After seven fastballs, six curveballs, four sweepers and one cutter, after 12 foul balls, two called strikes and dozens of check-ins on the runner at second base, Tristan Peters jogged to first base.

Peters’ 18-pitch clinic ended Gavin Williams’ Monday night and set the stage for a flurry of Chicago White Sox offense in their series-opening 7-3 victory against the team chasing them in the American League Central, the Cleveland Guardians. The win vaulted Chicago 1 1/2 games ahead of Cleveland in the division.

Williams had kept Chicago scoreless through five innings, navigating a tightrope as the White Sox kept placing runners on base. Andrew Benintendi opened the sixth with a single, and Williams was nearing the end of his outing anyway, given his pitch count had risen to 95. Peters made him work overtime.

“I felt like I was up there for an hour,” Peters said. “I was just exhausted. After, like, eight pitches, I was like, ‘OK, this is getting pretty long.’”

Peters recorded the plate appearance with the third-most pitches since 2000, according to the Elias Sports Bureau. In that span, it’s tied for the most pitches in a plate appearance that ended in a walk. San Francisco Giants first baseman Brandon Belt mounted a 21-pitch at-bat against the Los Angeles Angels in 2018, and St. Louis Cardinals catcher Matt Wieters forced 19 pitches from Minnesota Twins reliever Caleb Thielbar in 2020.

The encounter started with a curveball that appeared to clip the bottom of the strike zone but was called a ball. Catcher Patrick Bailey opted not to challenge. Williams then tossed a pair of fastballs on the inside corner for called strikes. Peters fouled off two fastballs, a curveball and a sweeper, took a curveball in the dirt, fouled off two fastballs, two curveballs, a sweeper and a cutter, watched a sweeper sail low out of the zone, fouled off a sweeper and a fastball and, finally, resisted a curveball off the plate.

“I counted at one point, and I just stopped counting because it was getting up there,” Williams said. “Those at-bats are frustrating, but props to him for the way he did that.”

With one more strikeout, Williams would have pulled into a tie with Jacob Misiorowski and Dylan Cease for the league lead.

Peters proved a pest to the Guardians again a few minutes later, as Colson Montgomery slapped a grounder to first base, but Cleveland’s Nathaniel Lowe struck Peters in the helmet on a throw to second in a bid to start a double play. The ball caromed into left field and allowed Benintendi to score.

“That was probably one of the best feelings ever,” Peters said.

That opened the floodgates, as Chase Meidroth delivered an RBI single, Kyle Teel supplied a two-run double and Miguel Vargas launched a two-run blast onto the left-field porch before the end of the inning.

With the win, the White Sox secured the season tiebreaker over the Guardians, so if the teams wind up with the same record, Chicago would win its first division title since 2021, and Cleveland would be left to fend for its playoff life in a crowded wild-card race. The Guardians can still take a half-game lead over the White Sox if they win the final two games of the series.
